description: Hand intrinsic muscles defined from data, on MyoHand's bodies (right-hand body frames; the left hand mirrors z, as myo_sim mirrors the arm): the thenar muscles, the two heads of the first dorsal interosseous and the hypothenar muscles (group). Architecture (PCSA, optimal fibre length, pennation) from Jacobson et al. 1992 Table I (n = 9), head splits as cited per row; peak force = PCSA x specific_tension unless a row says otherwise. Sites start at the cited source points (sites[*].start) and are fitted to published moment arms by scripts/generate_hand_intrinsic_muscles.py --fit (path_fit); sites[*].pos is the fitted position. All values SI except PCSA (cm2), moment arms (mm) and angles (deg). The model itself is the XML: sites in myoarm_r_chain.xml, tendons and muscles in the generated blocks of myoarm_r_tendon.xml and myoarm_r_muscle.xml, all written from this table by the same script. Rows with a block label are written in place of the hand-written element they replace, so actuator indices stay.

music2026.citation: Xu P, Ye Y, Sun S, Ding Y, Schumann E, Liu CK. MUSIC: Learning muscle-driven dexterous hand control. ACM Trans Graph 45(4), 2026 (arXiv:2604.23886).

music2026.provenance: MUSIC Appendix A: peak force and optimal fibre length from prior literature (Holzbaur et al. 2005; Del Santo et al. 2007), scaled as the other MyoHand muscles; attachments from anatomical atlases (Rohen et al. 2006; Standring et al. 2005); straight-line paths with via points.

mirakhorlo2016.location: Supplement 2: Table 3 (joint axes and pivots), Table 4 (landmarks), Table 7 (muscle points); one fresh-frozen female right arm; mm, ulnar-styloid frame, x radial, y proximal, z dorsal; main text Table 2 (p. 46): optimal fibre length, tendon length, pennation, mass and PCSA per muscle and head (PCSA = mass / (density x L_opt), no cos(pennation))

mirakhorlo2016.registration: The supplement's attachment points (Table 7) were mapped onto MyoHand by a similarity fit of the wrist, thumb CMC and MCP 2-5 joint centres (scale 0.978, rotation 7.8 deg, residual 1-10 mm), then per-segment frames for the phalanges; the mapped points are the fit start points (sites[*].start).

smutz1998.citation: Smutz WP, Kongsayreepong A, Hughes RE, Niebur G, Cooney WP, An KN. Mechanical advantage of the thumb muscles. J Biomech 31(6):565-570, 1998.
smutz1998.location: Tables 2-5 (pp. 567-568): moment arms of FPL, EPL, EPB, APL, FPB, APB, ADPt, ADPo and OPP at the MP and CMC joints over the measured ranges; 7 fresh-frozen hands, mean age 77. Positive = flexor / adductor. The abstract calls FPB an adductor; its tables and text show an abductor.

linscheid1991.note: Per-head values for DI1 (DIO1R = MC1 head, DIO1U = MC2 head), FPB, AdP and ADQ; PCSAs 2-3.5 times Jacobson 1992.

brandhollister1993.location: Ch. 12 pp. 294-296 and Fig. 12-39 (first dorsal interosseous); Table 14-4 p. 369 (in-vivo intrinsic force estimates)

salsbury1937.location: Table I pp. 397-399 (per hand), Table II p. 400 (summary: share of tendon to expansion vs bone; 28 specimens per muscle, embalmed)

an1979.citation: An KN, Chao EY, Cooney WP, Linscheid RL. Normative model of human hand for biomechanical analysis. J Biomech 12(10):775-788, 1979.
an1979.location: Table 1 (p. 776: 'ulnar interosseous (UI)' at the MP of every finger), Table 6 (p. 784: little-finger moment potentials, UL-I flexion 0.271, ulnar bending -0.495, axial -0.104, normalised by the middle-phalanx length), Table 11 (p. 786: little-finger tendon locations)

santoneto1984.citation: Santo Neto H, de Carvalho VC, Penteado CV. The abductor digiti minimi muscle of the hand. Okajimas Folia Anat Jpn 60:389-400, 1984.

patil2021.citation: Patil RK, Malhotra G, Tsai TM. Assessing the usability of flexor digiti minimi muscle for opponensplasty: an anatomic study. J Hand Surg Am 46(10):925.e1-925.e5, 2021.

lee2015.citation: Lee JH, Asakawa DS, Dennerlein JT, Jindrich DL. Finger muscle attachments for an OpenSim upper-extremity model. PLoS ONE 10(4):e0121712, 2015; correction PLoS ONE 17:e0267620, 2022.
lee2015.location: Methods (muscle list), Table 6 (moment arms), Table 10 (digit-5 tendon locations, from An et al. 1979)

specific_tension.derivation: least squares F = sigma x PCSA over MyoHand's OP (180 N), EPB (46.0 N) and APL (116.7 N) with Jacobson 1992 PCSA 1.02, 0.47, 1.93 cm2; per muscle 176.5, 97.9, 60.5 N/cm2, so MyoHand implies no single value and the fitted one is a compromise (forces scale linearly with it).
specific_tension.status: kept for this table until the common intrinsic specific tension is decided; 55 N/cm2 (O'Brien et al. 2010, Mirakhorlo et al. 2018) is the proposed value

path_fit.method: Least squares on the site positions (each site within +- bound_m of its start, per coordinate) of the residuals (model - mean) / max(SD, sd_floor_mm) at every tabled posture, plus |site - start| / regularisation_m per coordinate. Moment arms are MuJoCo dL/dq (central differences). Rows with the same fit.group are fitted together; their moment arms are force-weighted means. Constraint (penalty): the normalised fibre length (L - l_ts) / L_fo, with the Barry et al. 2018 Eq. 1 slack length, stays within fibre_length_window over the measurement box and below full_range_max over the full ranges of the crossed joints (which bounds the passive force at the ends of the ranges; MuJoCo's passive force reaches about 2 F_max at 1.6). In a group of heads, each head is held (penalty, 1 per mm) to the sign of every group target of at least 2 mm, so no head turns against its muscle. Rows whose fit carries reference instead of targets are not fitted to them (only the window and the regularisation act) and report their reference moment arms.
path_fit.posture: Smutz 1998 neutral = mid-point of the thumb CMC ranges (thumb at the radial side of the index DIP) = mid-point of MyoHand's cmc_flexion_r and cmc_abduction_r ranges; MP and IP at 0. posture_deg are anatomical (flexion, abduction positive) offsets from it: cmc_flexion_r q = q_mid - deg (MyoHand +q extends), cmc_abduction_r q = q_mid + deg, mp_flexion_r q = -deg. Signs of the targets: positive = flexor / adductor, equal to MyoHand's dL/dq.
path_fit.measurement_box: thumb: the Smutz posture box (CMC 20 deg flexion to 25 deg extension, 20 deg abduction to 20 deg adduction, MP 10 deg hyperextension to 40 deg flexion); index: MCP2 flexion 0-90 deg and abduction +-15 deg, with the thumb box for DI1s; little finger: MCP5 flexion 0-90 deg and abduction +-15 deg, CMC5 -10.3 to 33 deg for muscles that arise proximal of MC5

force_N.derivation: 180 N, MyoHand's value, kept until the intrinsic specific tension is decided (1.02 cm2 x 86.3 N/cm2 would give 88.0 N; 180 N implies 176.5 N/cm2)

muscles.name: AdPt
muscles.anatomy: adductor pollicis, transverse head (from the palmar ridge of the MC3 shaft)

force_N.derivation: 1.94 cm2 x 1.18 / 3.19 (Stamenkovic 2014 head ratio) = 0.718 cm2 x 86.3 N/cm2

head_split.note: Jacobson's total AdP PCSA split by Stamenkovic's head ratio (n = 10), so the total force (167.5 N) is the single head's. Mirakhorlo 2016 Table 2 (n = 1): 0.53 / 1.29 cm2, the same direction.

fit.note: Not fitted to Smutz 1998: with MyoHand's thumb CMC axes no site shift reproduces the Smutz adduction trend (model arms grow toward adduction, Smutz's shrink), and fitting the AdP heads to the Smutz flexion arms trades away their adduction arm, after which the lateral pinch of the hand-function validation has no solution within its off-axis limit (relaxed: 20.5 N at 1.9 x off-axis). The heads keep the registered Mirakhorlo 2016 paths, moved only as far as the fibre-length window requires; the Smutz values are reported in fit.result.reference_mm.

muscles.name: FPBs
muscles.anatomy: flexor pollicis brevis, superficial head (median nerve; from the flexor retinaculum and trapezium)

start.source: radial sesamoid level: start at MUSIC's APB via point (music2026)

force_N.derivation: 0.66 cm2 x 0.56 (Mirakhorlo 2016 head ratio, n = 1) = 0.37 cm2 x 86.3 N/cm2

head_split.note: Mirakhorlo 2016 Table 2 (n = 1): superficial 0.21, deep 0.165 cm2. Linscheid 1991 (n = 8) gives 0.62 / 0.38; Karademir 2022 in-vivo CSA 1.0 / 0.8 cm2.

fit.note: Smutz measured FPB as one muscle: the force-weighted mean of both heads is fitted.

muscles.name: AdPo
muscles.anatomy: adductor pollicis, oblique head (from the capitate and the bases of MC2-3)

force_N.derivation: 1.94 cm2 x 2.01 / 3.19 (Stamenkovic 2014 head ratio) = 1.222 cm2 x 86.3 N/cm2

fit.note: Not fitted to Smutz 1998: with MyoHand's thumb CMC axes no site shift reproduces the Smutz adduction trend (model arms grow toward adduction, Smutz's shrink), and fitting the AdP heads to the Smutz flexion arms trades away their adduction arm, after which the lateral pinch of the hand-function validation has no solution within its off-axis limit (relaxed: 20.5 N at 1.9 x off-axis). The heads keep the registered Mirakhorlo 2016 paths, moved only as far as the fibre-length window requires; the Smutz values are reported in fit.result.reference_mm.

muscles.name: FPBd
muscles.anatomy: flexor pollicis brevis, deep head (ulnar nerve; from the trapezoid and capitate)

start.source: radial sesamoid level, next to the superficial head's via point (assumed)

force_N.derivation: 0.66 cm2 x 0.44 (Mirakhorlo 2016 head ratio, n = 1) = 0.29 cm2 x 86.3 N/cm2

muscles.name: DI1d
muscles.anatomy: first dorsal interosseous, deep head (from the radial MC2 shaft); bony insertion on the PP2 base

force_N.derivation: 1.5 cm2 x 0.64 (Mirakhorlo 2016 head ratio, n = 1) = 0.96 cm2 x 86.3 N/cm2

head_split.note: Mirakhorlo 2016 Table 2 (n = 1): MC1 head 0.62, MC2 head 1.11 cm2. Linscheid 1991 (n = 8) gives 0.50 / 0.50.

muscles.insertion_note: Bony (PP2 base): Salsbury 1937 wholly bony in 28/28 hands, Masquelet 1986 (34 hands), Eladoumikdachi 2002 lateral band 2/14.

mcp2_flexion_r.where: Table 3 (RI, index; averaged over the range)

fit.note: An 1983's RI is the whole first dorsal interosseous: the force-weighted mean of both heads is fitted (negative dL/dq: flexor, radial abductor). Masquelet 1986: the deep head is the main MCP flexor, the superficial head the main abductor (soft ordering constraints). Brand & Hollister 1993: the superficial head adds little to thumb motion; its CMC adduction arm is fitted to 2 +- 2 mm (a judgement band, not a measurement).

muscles.name: DI1s
muscles.anatomy: first dorsal interosseous, superficial head (from the ulnar MC1 shaft); crosses the thumb CMC

force_N.derivation: 1.5 cm2 x 0.36 (Mirakhorlo 2016 head ratio, n = 1) = 0.54 cm2 x 86.3 N/cm2

cmc_abduction_r.note: judgement band at the Smutz neutral

muscles.name: ADM
muscles.anatomy: abductor digiti minimi (from the pisiform; insertion on the ulnar base of the proximal phalanx)

start.source: ulnar-palmar of the MC5 head: start at the former UI_UB5 via point (caggiano2022), so the tendon follows the bone in MCP flexion

muscles.identity_note: UI_UB5 played the ulnar abductor of digit 5 but arose from MC3 at the CMC5 level and inserted into the ulnar lateral band; ADM arises from the pisiform in 50/50 hands and reaches the dorsal aponeurosis in 16 % (Santo Neto 1984). An 1979 names the MP intrinsic on the ulnar side of every finger 'ulnar interosseous'; on digit 5 only ADM lies there (our identification).

mcp5_abduction_r.where: Table 6 p. 784, little-finger ulnar intrinsic: ulnar bending potential 0.495 x middle-phalanx length (MyoHand 21.0 mm)
mcp5_abduction_r.sd_note: no spread published; 2 mm is a fit tolerance

mcp5_flexion_r.where: Table 6 p. 784: flexion potential 0.271 x middle-phalanx length (a flexor: negative dL/dq)
mcp5_flexion_r.sd_note: no spread published; 2 mm is a fit tolerance

muscles.name: FDM
muscles.anatomy: flexor digiti minimi brevis (from the hook of the hamate; insertion on the ulnar-palmar base of the proximal phalanx)

start.source: palmar of the MC5 head (assumed), so the tendon follows the bone in MCP flexion

muscles.presence_note: absent in 10 of 30 hands and much smaller than ADM in 4 more (Patil 2021); modelled as present (Jacobson's n = 9 mean).

fit.note: No moment arm of FDM is published; the registered path is kept (moved only as far as the fibre-length window requires) and checked for sign (MCP5 and CMC5 flexor).

muscles.name: ODM
muscles.anatomy: opponens digiti minimi (from the hook of the hamate; insertion along the ulnar border of the MC5 shaft); crosses only CMC5

fit.note: No moment arm of ODM is published; validated by the active cupping it produces with FDM and ADM (Büren et al. 2020 / Al Maktary 2019 maxima).

joint_name_note: MUSIC's thumb CMC joints have the same axes as MyoHand's but swapped names: MUSIC cmc_flexion = myo_sim cmc_abduction_r and vice versa. Sites are body-relative, so the geometry transfers unchanged (lengths and moment arms match MUSIC to 1e-11 m with the names mapped).

passive_fit.method: fpmax (MuJoCo's passive-force scale) of every row that crosses a joint of these passive rows (thumb, little-finger MCP and CMC5), fitted with the extrinsic muscles' loss of fit_muscle_passive.py to the measured total passive moments of these rows of passive_joint_moments.json, over each row's fit range, other joints at 0, counting only the muscles a row's source includes (subtract_model_muscles.muscles) where it names them; the joint springs are fitted afterwards to the remainder. MuJoCo's passive force-length curve (class default fpmax 1.3) is much stiffer than measured curves, as for the extrinsic muscles.
